trace.content:
You write job advertisements for a South African recruitment platform. You receive a hiring brief and return one advertisement as structured JSON.

The only source of facts is the brief. This rule is absolute:
- Every statement about the employer, pay, benefits, location, work mode, team, reporting line, process, dates or legal status must appear in the brief. If the brief does not state it, leave the field empty. Never invent a benefit, a salary, a team size, a closing date, a contact, or an equity, privacy or accessibility statement.
- You may rephrase, reorder, split and tighten the brief's content. You may not add facts.
- If the brief is thin, write a shorter ad. A short true ad beats a long padded one.

Write for the candidate reading on a phone:
- Title: the plain occupation name, under 60 characters, no internal grade codes, no words like rockstar or ninja.
- 300–650 words in total. Sentences under 25 words. Short paragraphs; bullets for duties, requirements and benefits.
- Address the reader as "you". Never write "the ideal candidate", "the successful applicant" or "he/she".
- If the brief gives a purpose or success measures, use them to tell the reader what they will own and what good looks like. If a requirement carries "needed because", you may state that reason.
- Each responsibility bullet names a specific activity and its object, and where the brief allows, its scale, audience or how success is measured. Not "support the team"; rather "reconcile 40 supplier statements each month and resolve queries with buyers".
- Three to six must-have requirements, each one needed by a duty you listed. Everything else goes under nice-to-have. Do not add years-of-experience figures the brief did not give.
- If pay is given, state it exactly, with what determines placement in the range if the brief says so.
- Say who the person reports to and the team size only if the brief gives them. Say remote, hybrid or on-site only if the brief does.
- Plain language. No "fast-paced", "work hard play hard", "self-starter", "rockstar", "passionate", "competitive salary", "market-related".
- Neutral wording: avoid aggressive, dominant, competitive, fearless and similar masculine-coded adjectives; avoid "young", "energetic", "recent graduate", "native speaker", "able-bodied", age ranges, and anything about family status, religion or health. State a requirement only if the duties need it.
- Include the employer's equity, POPIA and accessibility statements verbatim when the brief provides them; otherwise leave those fields empty.
- Include application steps, closing date and contact only as given. If the brief says the ad is published on a job board with its own Apply button, leave the contact field empty.

Output: the JSON structure requested, with empty strings, 0 or "unspecified" for anything the brief does not provide.

Title: Head of Finance – Technology & Digital
Company: Absa Group
About the company: Empowering Africa’s tomorrow, together…one story at a time. With over 100 years of rich history and strongly positioned as a local bank with regional and international expertise, a career with our family offers the opportunity to be part of this exciting growth journey, to reset our future and shape our destiny as a proudly African group.
Purpose of the role: To provide strategic financial leadership and commercial challenge to the Business Banking Technology & Digital function, ensuring technology expenditure, investments and architecture decisions deliver measurable business value. The role will provide end-to-end financial oversight across technology run costs, infrastructure, cloud, applications, software and licensing, technology vendors and strategic change. It will translate complex technology decisions into clear financial and commercial insights that enable informed investment, prioritisation and cost optimisation.
Responsibilities (hiring manager's notes):
  - Own financial planning, forecasting and performance management for the Technology portfolio.
  - Develop transparency of technology costs across applications, platforms, infrastructure, vendors and business services.
  - Establish clear views of Run vs Change expenditure and key cost drivers.
  - Understand and challenge technology allocations and consumption-based charges.
  - Develop Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) and unit-cost perspectives for major technology services.
  - Identify structural cost optimisation opportunities rather than relying only on tactical budget reductions.
  - Partner Technology executives on investment prioritisation and portfolio decisions.
  - Build and challenge business cases across cloud migration, application modernisation, automation, digital platforms and technology transformation.
  - Evaluate NPV, IRR, payback, P&L, cash-flow and balance-sheet implications of investments.
  - Monitor benefits realisation against approved investment cases.
  - Provide financial challenge on build vs buy, migrate vs retain and invest vs decommission decisions.
  - Build sufficient understanding of Azure/AWS economics to challenge cloud consumption and optimisation opportunities.
  - Understand consumption-based pricing, tagging and allocation methodologies.
  - Partner Technology teams to improve transparency of cloud spend and accountability.
  - Identify opportunities to optimise cloud utilisation and reduce inefficient consumption.
  - Understand the financial implications of cloud migration and architecture decisions.
  - Develop financial views at application/platform/service level, not only cost-centre level.
  - Integrate application run costs, infrastructure, licences, vendor expenditure and change investment to determine full economic cost.
  - Identify duplicate, underutilised or high-cost applications and platforms.
  - Support application rationalisation and decommissioning decisions.
  - Translate technology architecture choices into understandable financial consequences.
  - Provide financial challenge on technology contracts, software licensing, SaaS, outsourcing and professional services.
  - Analyse vendor cost trends and commercial commitments.
  - Support contract renewal and commercial negotiation decisions.
  - Challenge licence utilisation, demand and unit pricing.
  - Assess the long-term TCO implications of major vendor and platform choices.
  - Establish a stronger connection between: Technology spend → technology performance → customer/business outcome → financial value
  - Develop decision-quality reporting through Power BI and advanced Excel.
  - Analyse large datasets to identify technology cost drivers and optimisation opportunities.
  - Create executive dashboards linking financial and technology KPIs.
  - Perform scenario, sensitivity and driver-based modelling.
  - Translate complex technology financial information into concise Exco-level insights.
  - Use data to move Finance from retrospective reporting toward forward-looking commercial insight.
  - Act as a credible financial adviser to BB CIO and Technology leadership.
  - Constructively challenge technology investment, architecture and sourcing decisions.
  - Translate technical discussions into financial and commercial implications.
  - Influence decisions through fact-based analysis rather than financial control alone.
  - Connect Technology priorities to BB strategy, customer outcomes, productivity and financial objectives.
Must-have requirements:
  - Technology financial management
  - FP&A, budgeting and forecasting
  - Business-case development
  - Investment appraisal
  - TCO modelling
  - Cost allocation and driver-based costing
  - Benefits realisation
  - Capex/Opex and capitalisation understanding
  - Commercial/vendor analysis
  - Advanced financial modelling
  - Technology Business Management (TBM) concepts
  - FinOps / cloud economics
  - Application economics
  - Technology cost-allocation methodologies
  - Software and licensing economics
  - Technology vendor management
  - Understanding of infrastructure and cloud services
  - Technology change/investment lifecycle
  - Postgraduate Degrees and Professional Qualifications: Financial Sciences (Required)
Nice-to-have:
  - APIs and integration
  - SaaS
  - Databases and compute
  - Cloud vs on-premise architecture
  - Cybersecurity and resilience
  - Digital platforms
  - AI and automation economics
  - Application rationalisation and technical debt
Location: Sandton
Team notes: Business Banking Technology & Digital function; partners with BB CIO and Technology leadership
Employment equity statement: Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
Accessibility statement: We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.
Note: the ad will be published on a job board with its own Apply button.

• Use Azure and AWS economics, consumption-based pricing, tagging and allocation methods to improve cloud spend transparency and reduce inefficient consumption.

• Identify duplicate, underutilised or high-cost applications and support rationalisation and decommissioning decisions.
• Provide financial challenge on technology contracts, software licensing, SaaS, outsourcing and professional services, and support renewals and commercial negotiations.
• Produce decision-quality reporting in Power BI and advanced Excel, including executive dashboards linking financial and technology KPIs, and scenario, sensitivity and driver-based models.
• Advise the BB CIO and Technology leadership, translating technical discussions into commercial implications and connecting technology spend to performance, customer outcomes and financial value.

What you need
• Technology financial management, including FP&A, budgeting and forecasting
• Business-case development, investment appraisal, TCO modelling and benefits realisation
• Cost allocation and driver-based costing, plus Capex/Opex and capitalisation understanding
• Technology Business Management (TBM) concepts, FinOps and cloud economics, application economics, and software and licensing economics
• Commercial and vendor analysis, technology vendor management, and advanced financial modelling

• Postgraduate degree or professional qualification in Financial Sciences (required)

Nice to have
• APIs and integration
• SaaS
• Databases and compute
• Cloud versus on-premise architecture
• Cybersecurity and resilience
• Digital platforms
• AI and automation economics
• Application rationalisation and technical debt

We encourage applicants who may require reasonable accommodation during the recruitment process to let us know so that appropriate support can be provided.

Absa is committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone can thrive. We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applications from suitably qualified individuals from diverse backgrounds. In support of our Diversity, Equity, Inclusion and Belonging (DEIB) commitments and Employment Equity objectives, preference may be given to candidates from underrepresented designated groups, including persons with disabilities.
